legend_intro: Every claim in this report carries a label that says how it is known.
legend_ids: File paths, function names and code are never translated. Line numbers refer to the analysed commit; stale references are flagged.
v_verified-source_desc: Read directly from the code at the cited lines (parsed, not guessed).
v_structurally-inferred_desc: Reasoned from code structure (e.g. a method matched by name). Likely, but not proven.
v_test-verified_desc: Backed by a test that was actually executed and passed in a recorded run.
v_runtime-observed_desc: Seen in a real, instrumented execution of the program.
v_partially-verified_desc: Some parts are confirmed; others still need checking.
v_not-verified_desc: Stated without proof; treat as a hypothesis.
nav_hint: Tip: every path:line link opens the exact source lines.
no_description: No project description found in the manifests.
auto_summary: Mostly **{lang}** ({share}% of analysed lines). Frameworks detected: {fw}. {entries} entry point(s), {routes} route(s), {tests} test file(s).
auto_summary_note: This summary is generated from manifests and parsed code. An agent-written explanation appears here once added.
layer_hint_note: Layer hints come from folder naming conventions (inferred). Graph edges come from real imports and calls.
env_vars_note: Only names are shown. Values are never read or stored.
calls_resolution: {unresolved} of {total} call sites could not be resolved statically (dynamic calls, callbacks, third-party objects).
limitations_static: Static analysis cannot see dependency injection, reflection, config-driven wiring or runtime registration. Unexplored areas are listed above.
md_lang_summary: Mostly **{lang}** ({share}% of analysed lines; {files} files, {lines} lines).
arch_sub: Modules and files connected by real import and call edges. Click a node for details; double-click a module to open its files.
arch_help: Node size reflects lines of code. Red nodes are part of an import cycle.
arch_select: Select a node to inspect its incoming and outgoing relationships.
flows_sub: Step through a source-backed execution path. Each step shows the exact code responsible.
flow_static_note: Reconstructed from source code (inferred). This is not a recording of a real run.
flow_unresolved_note: {n} step(s) could not be resolved statically; the real path may differ.
lane_diagram: Which file each step runs in
scenarios_note: Terminal outcomes found in the flow and the nearest conditions guarding them (inferred).
no_outcomes: No terminal outcomes found in this flow.
no_flows: No flows yet. Ask the agent to trace a feature, or run:
code_sub: Browse embedded source. Links from anywhere in the report open here with lines highlighted.
pick_file: Pick a file on the left, or follow a path:line link.
not_embedded: Source not embedded in this report (size budget). Open it in your editor:
resolved_edges_only: Only statically resolved edges are listed.
learn_sub: Explanations written for you, each tied to exact source lines. Pick your depth.
translation_missing: This explanation is not available in the selected language yet; showing English.
no_explanations: No explanations yet. The agent adds them with
contribute_sub: Everything you need to change this code safely: where it lives, who calls it, what tests cover it, and what is still unknown.
context_note: Statuses describe what the engine located. Mark an area reviewed only after reading its evidence.
ready_1: I can explain what the code does today, citing the lines.
ready_2: I have read every direct caller.
ready_3: I know which tests cover it and have run them.
ready_4: I have considered the branch conditions and error paths.
ready_5: I follow the repository's existing conventions.
ready_6: I can explain what my change does and why.
no_changes: No change analysis yet. After editing code, run:
changes_summary: Compared with `{baseline}`: {added} added, {modified} modified, {deleted} deleted file(s); {syms} symbol(s) changed; {impacted} symbol(s) impacted.
sim_sub: Explore behaviour at three levels of certainty. Each level is labelled; they are never mixed.
sim_l1_desc: Possible paths reconstructed from code. Useful for learning; not proof of behaviour.
sim_l2_desc: Results of tests that were actually executed (with the user's approval). Only executed tests are reported.
sim_l3_desc: Function calls recorded while the program really ran under instrumentation.
no_test_runs: No test runs recorded. Plan and (after approval) run tests:
no_runtime: No runtime traces yet. With approval, run:
df_sub: How requests come in, which parts of the code they pass through, and where data is stored or sent. The moving dots show which way calls and data travel.
df_no_storages: No databases, caches, files or external services were found in the parsed imports.
df_empty: There is nothing to draw yet. Run a scan first:
df_replay_none: This flow stays inside one component, so there is no hop to animate on the map.
df_no_flows: Trace a flow first to replay it on the map:
df_detail_hint: Click a component or a storage to see what it talks to, with the source lines that prove each connection.
df_note: Components and storages come from parsed imports and external calls. Columns come from entry points, routes and handlers (verified) or from folder names (inferred). Dynamic wiring such as dependency injection, reflection or config-driven plugins is not shown.
stage_title: Request journey: each hop is one step
df_basis_frontend: frontend code: .jsx/.tsx/.vue/.svelte files or a frontend folder (inferred)
df_basis_models: its files import a database package (models / data access)
